art.subject: Large Hawk-Cuckoo (Hierococcyx sparverioides), adult, as seen in Korean woodland in late spring: head slate-grey, darker on the face; chin dark grey; throat whitish; upperparts plain grey-brown; upper breast rufous with dark streaks; lower breast and belly white, barred dark brown; undertail coverts white; tail long, grey-brown with broad blackish bars and a pale tip; bill dark with a yellowish base; yellow eye-ring and yellow-orange iris; legs yellow.
art.pose: perched upright on a branch inside the canopy, side view
art.scene: Korean broadleaf forest in late spring (May–June), fresh green foliage and dappled light; no people, buildings or text
views: adult (sexes alike), perched upright on a branch inside the canopy, side view: hawk-like cuckoo with a grey head contrasting with plain brown upperparts, short slightly decurved bill, rufous upper breast with dark streaks, white lower breast and belly barred dark brown, long tail with broad dark bands
adult, perched upright, three-quarter front view: grey head, rufous dark-streaked upper breast, white belly with dark brown bars, long tail with broad dark bands hanging straight down
art.build: Large, hawk-like cuckoo, slightly larger than Common Cuckoo and shaped like a sparrowhawk, with a long, broad tail with a rounded tip, rounded wings and a fairly upright posture when perched. Bill short and slightly decurved. Legs short, yellow, with two toes forward and two back. In flight broad-winged, with fast shallow wingbeats and short glides, easily mistaken for an Accipiter.
avoid: Do not paint a plain, unstreaked pale orange breast, a white nape patch and a slate-grey back; that is Northern Hawk-Cuckoo (Hierococcyx hyperythrus).
Do not give it a hooked raptor bill or strong talons; it has a small cuckoo bill and weak feet.
Do not paint the whole underparts finely barred grey like Common Cuckoo; the upper breast is rufous and streaked.
Do not paint a dark eye without a yellow eye-ring.
